newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish external reserves down 691 mln punts in Nov.
newsitem.headline: Irish external reserves down 691 mln punts in Nov.

text.p: Ireland's official external reserves fell by 691 million Irish pounds to 5.339 billion at the end of November, central bank monthly statistics showed on Thursday.

"Negative foreign exchange market interventions added to interest and principal payments on the Exchequer foreign debt exceeded EU receipts to account for most of the reduction," the central bank said.
In addition, a valuation adjustment caused the official external reserves to be 200 million punts lower than they would otherwise have been, the bank said.
The Net External Liability (NEL) of all credit institutions fell by 1.173 billion pounds in November, reversing an increase the previous month, the central bank said.
An increase in banks' resident foreign currency desposits and a fall in their resident foreign currency lending contributed to the trend, it said.
Irish pound credit to the government from domestic credit institutions increased by 138 million punts in the month.
Holdings of Exchequer notes rose by 56 million while holdings of government bonds increased by 80 million but non-resident holdings of Irish government securities fell by 164 million punts.
